description: We are an aerospace engineering team combining expertise in MATLAB simulation, Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD), and 3D CAD modeling to tackle microgravity combustion. Our goal is to build an SI-powered fire safety dashboard for deep-space habitats (ISS, Moon, Mars) by analyzing NASA's Saffire and BASS datasets to rank material flammability and simulate flame spread under varying ventilation regimes.
summary:
We developed "Flame in Freefall," an interactive web dashboard featuring a real-time microgravity flammability physics engine and an integrated Super Intelligence (SI) Safety Copilot. Built as a deployment-ready HTML/JavaScript tool, our solution allows users to instantly evaluate the fire risk of spacecraft materials under various atmospheric conditions without requiring complex backend server installations.

To address the Space Apps challenge, our physics engine directly leverages microgravity combustion data from NASA's Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) database—specifically the Saffire and BASS-II experiments. By adjusting interactive sliders for cabin pressure, oxygen concentration, and ventilation airflow, the tool mathematically models the resulting Fire Risk Index (FRI) for spacecraft materials like PMMA and SIBAL Fabric. The integrated Gemini SI Copilot acts in tandem with the physics engine to translate these complex datasets into actionable, immediate engineering analysis.

This project is crucial for advancing human space exploration safety. Fire behavior in zero gravity is highly counterintuitive; while ventilation provides necessary oxygen, excessive airflow can induce aerodynamic stretch and reach a blowout limit that extinguishes the flame. By providing engineers and mission planners with a visual risk assessment tool that maps these thresholds, our dashboard actively aids in the design of safer lunar habitats and life support systems.
details:
FLAME IN FREEFALL: MICROGRAVITY FIRE SAFETY & PREDICTIVE HAZARD DASHBOARD

What exactly does it do? "Flame in Freefall" is a standalone, interactive web dashboard designed to evaluate spacecraft material flammability in zero-gravity environments. It features a real-time physics engine that calculates a Fire Risk Index (FRI) for materials like PMMA and SIBAL Fabric based on live environmental parameters. Additionally, it integrates a Super Intelligence (SI) Safety Copilot to provide instant engineering analysis and hazard mitigation guidance.

How does it work? The dashboard operates entirely on the client-side using a lightweight HTML/JS architecture. Users adjust sliders for Cabin Pressure, Oxygen Concentration, and Ventilation Airflow. The physics engine processes these inputs through mathematical models derived from NASA's Saffire and BASS-II experiments, calculating how forced convection initially accelerates flame spread before reaching a critical "blowout limit." The integrated SI Copilot connects to the Gemini API (with a built-in offline failsafe) to translate these complex physics into natural language safety assessments.

What benefits does it have? Fire behavior in microgravity is highly counterintuitive; cool flames and forced convection completely alter ignition thresholds. Our tool eliminates the guesswork by providing mission planners and aerospace engineers with a dynamic, visual hazard scoring system. Because it is a zero-install HTML file, it is instantly accessible and deployable on any standard browser without complex backend server dependencies.

What do you hope to achieve? We aim to advance human spaceflight safety for the Artemis generation and beyond. By transforming raw, complex microgravity combustion datasets into an intuitive, predictive UI, we hope to accelerate the design of safer lunar habitats and life support systems, ensuring astronauts are protected from unforeseen fire hazards.

What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use?

  • Coding Languages: HTML, CSS, and vanilla JavaScript (for the physics engine and UI).
  • Super Intelligence (SI): Google Gemini 1.5 Flash API (for the SI Safety Copilot).
  • Engineering Software: CATIA V5 (for 3D lunar habitat interior modeling and forced airflow visualization) and MATLAB (for plotting and verifying the microgravity FRI parabolic curves).
  • Datasets: NASA Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) database, specifically the Saffire, BASS-II, and FLEX experiments.
